reconcile.note: Gill ties John 14:19's 'no more' to a time limit ending precisely at the parousia, when every eye, echoing Revelation 1:7, will see Christ return.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible lists this pairing as a contradiction, since the world seeing Jesus no more clashes with the promise that every eye will see him return.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also.
sides.verseText: Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also.

sides.snippet: Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen.
sides.verseText: Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen.
